Meaning: To be fully absorbed in the story described in Shrimad Bhagwat means to be in constant association with the Supreme Lord Krishna.
And such association means to be free from material qualities. God
Shri Krishna is like the sun, and is equivalent to the darkness of material impurity. Just as in the presence of the sun,
darkness disappears, similarly, the constant companionship of Lord Shri Krishna is the one that removes the impurity of material qualities. The accumulation of physical qualities is the cause of repeated birth and death, and from physical qualities,
liberation is to be beyond qualities (Sattva). Because of knowing this secret of liberation, Maharaj Parikshit had now
self-realization because Srila Shukdev Goswami had told the king that the ultimate
achievement is inherent in the remembrance of Narayan at the time of death.
Maharaj Parikshit had to give up his body after seven days.
Therefore, he decided to give up his body by remembering God through the story of Shrimad Bhagwat,
and thus, by being fully alert before Lord Shri Krishna, he decided to give up his body. Those who listen to Shrimad Bhagwat in a practical way, their listening is different from Maharaj Parikshit's divine listening.
By doing so, it is different. King Parikshit had a vision of the supreme truth, Lord Shri Krishna. A materialistic person is not a free-spirited one; he wants to gain some material benefit by listening to the Shrimad Bhagavatam. Undoubtedly, such listeners, by listening to the Srimad Bhagavatam from a Vrittikavachak, can gain some material
benefits, but it does not mean that listening to the artificial Srimad Bhagavatam for a week is as beneficial as listening by Maharaj Parikshit.

It is the duty of a thoughtful person to listen to the Srimad Bhagavatam from a self-realized person and
not to be deceived by worldly people.
A person should keep listening to Shrimad Bhagwat in this way until the last moment of their life, so that they can truly attain the divine association of God and thus be liberated. Although Maharaj Parikshit had already renounced his kingdom and family, which are the embodiment of materialism,
even then, he was conscious of his physical body. They were constantly
wanting to be free from such bondage through the company of God.
